gen-gf-bellota-gf-fjord-one: Bellota's hanging-ended s gives it away at once. Fjord One follows as a text serif with wide round letters and a gentle swell in the bowls, so paragraphs move along smoothly beneath the pen-line heading.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-gentium-book-plus: Distinctive, stencil-like and drawn at a single width: that is Bellota. Gentium Book Plus, a classic serif, lightens its horizontals and tapers its strokes only slightly, so a long passage settles into a traditional, wide-mouthed rhythm.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-gfs-didot: GFS Didot is the literary voice here, with a restrained swell in its curves and generous gaps. Bellota, hanging its s ends far from the spine, has no swelling anywhere, so a longer passage reads as steady text serif beneath it.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-hahmlet: No modulation at all marks Bellota, every stroke traced like one stylus line. And Hahmlet, a text serif with a faint charcoal-like pressure shadow, handles the dignified running text that the display face leaves alone.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-im-fell-english-sc: IM Fell English SC sits in a middle path between monoline and razor-thin strokes, with open throats. But Bellota, bent-pipe constant in width with an s that hangs wide, is the one to carry display weight, while the text serif does the bookish reading.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-inria-serif: Pen-line boldness, hanging s and all. Bellota commands attention with unswelling curves, and Inria Serif, a text serif with slight bowl swell and lighter diagonals, handles the refined, dignified reading.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-joan: Joan is a classic serif with gentle weight shifts in its bowls and a clearly visible c. Its lighter but never threadlike horizontals meet Bellota's unvarying strokes, and that mix of plain-line display and softly shaded text is the pair's greatest draw.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-junge: Authoritative is the mood Bellota sets, with its far-hanging s and a line that never swells or tapers. Big and short is where it earns its keep, while Junge adds a mild pen-like variation in its serif.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-kameron: Pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin make Bellota instantly recognizable, its s ends drifting far from the spine. And Kameron, a serif with moderately weighty stems and curves that refuse to close, gives that stark heading a bookish companion.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-libertinus-serif: Refined is Libertinus Serif's mood, and Bellota's cord-heavy curves are far more insistent. Bellota is best at stating things loudly with that hanging s, while the text serif does its best work in soft, understated swells and an open s.
